questions.stem: If \(5x - 6 = 19\), what is the value of \(3x\)?
questions.explanation:
There is no need to find \(x\) first. Solve for \(5x\), then scale.
$$\begin{aligned}5x - 6 &= 19 \\ 5x &= 25 \\ x &= 5\end{aligned}$$
Therefore \(3x = 3(5) = 15\).

questions.stem:
$$3(x-4) = 2x+5$$
What value of \(x\) is the solution to the given equation?
questions.explanation:
Distribute and collect like terms.
$$\begin{aligned}3x - 12 &= 2x + 5 \\ x &= 17\end{aligned}$$

questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(x^2 + 2x - 15\)?
questions.explanation:
Find two numbers that multiply to \(-15\) and add to \(2\). Those numbers are \(5\) and \(-3\).
$$x^2 + 2x - 15 = (x+5)(x-3)$$

questions.stem:
$$x^2-5x=14$$
Which of the following is a solution to the given equation?
questions.explanation:
Set the equation equal to zero and factor.
$$\begin{aligned}x^2 - 5x - 14 &= 0 \\ (x-7)(x+2) &= 0\end{aligned}$$
By the Zero Product Property, \(x = 7\) or \(x = -2\). Of the answer choices, \(x = 7\) is a solution.

questions.stem:
The values in the data set shown represent the number of hours several students spent studying for an exam.
$$3,\ 8,\ 12,\ 5,\ 9,\ 1,\ 7$$
What is the median number of hours spent studying?
questions.explanation:
To find the median, arrange the values in order from least to greatest and identify the middle value.
$$1,\ 3,\ 5,\ \mathbf{7},\ 8,\ 9,\ 12$$
There are \(7\) values, so the median is the \(4\)th value: \(7\).

questions.stem: In the figure, lines \(l\) and \(m\) are parallel. What is the value of \(x\)?
questions.explanation:
Lines \(l\) and \(m\) are parallel. The angle marked \(x°\) and the angle marked \(62°\) are same-side interior angles (co-interior angles), which are supplementary when lines are parallel.
$$x + 62 = 180 \implies x = 118$$

questions.stem: Clare drives at a constant speed. After \(2\) hours of driving, she has traveled \(90\) miles. After \(5\) hours, she has traveled \(225\) miles. Which of the following equations models the distance \(d\), in miles, Clare has traveled after \(h\) hours of driving?
questions.explanation:
Since the speed is constant, find the rate of change.
$$\text{speed} = \frac{225-90}{5-2} = \frac{135}{3} = 45\text{ mph}$$
Since Clare starts from a distance of \(0\) miles, the equation is \(d = 45h\).

questions.stem: The graph of a function is shown in the \(xy\)-plane. Which of the following could be an equation for the function?
questions.explanation:
The graph shows a decreasing exponential function. This eliminates any equation with a base greater than \(1\), since those are increasing.
A) \(y = 50(1.3)^x\) has base \(1.3 > 1\) — increasing. Eliminate A.
B) \(y = 50(0.8)^x\) has base \(0.8 < 1\) — decreasing, with initial value \(50\). Keep B.
C) \(y = 100(0.7)^x\) is decreasing but has initial value \(100\), which does not match the graph. Eliminate C.
D) \(y = 100(1.2)^x\) has base \(1.2 > 1\) — increasing, and wrong initial value. Eliminate D.


The correct answer is B.

questions.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = \dfrac{3}{4}x - 6\). The graph of \(y = f(x)\) in the \(xy\)-plane has an \(x\)-intercept at \((a, 0)\). What is the value of \(a\)?
questions.explanation:
Set \(f(x) = 0\) and solve for \(x\).
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}x - 6 &= 0 \\ \frac{3}{4}x &= 6 \\ x &= 8\end{aligned}$$

questions.stem: Two research labs are collecting water samples for an environmental study. Lab A collects \(120\) samples per day and Lab B collects \(85\) samples per day. The study requires a combined total of at least \(2{,}000\) samples. If Lab A works for exactly \(10\) days, what is the minimum number of whole days Lab B must work to meet the study's requirement?
questions.explanation:
First find how many samples Lab A contributes after 10 days.
$$120 \times 10 = 1{,}200 \text{ samples}$$
Let \(d\) = the number of days Lab B works. Write and solve an inequality.
$$\begin{aligned}1{,}200 + 85d &\geq 2{,}000 \\ 85d &\geq 800 \\ d &\geq 9.41...\end{aligned}$$
The minimum number of whole days is \(10\).

questions.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = x^2 + 3\). The function \(g\) is defined by \(g(x) = f(x-2)\). What is the value of \(g(5)\)?
questions.explanation:
To find \(g(5)\), substitute \(x = 5\) into \(g(x) = f(x-2)\).
$$g(5) = f(5-2) = f(3) = 3^2 + 3 = 9 + 3 = 12$$

questions.stem: A car purchased for \$24{,}000 loses \(15\%\) of its value each year. Which of the following functions gives the value \(V\), in dollars, of the car \(t\) years after purchase?
questions.explanation:
A \(15\%\) decrease each year means the car retains \(85\%\) of its value, so it is multiplied by \(0.85\) each year.
$$V(t) = 24{,}000(0.85)^t$$
Check: at \(t=1\), \(V = 24{,}000(0.85) = 20{,}400\), a decrease of \(\$3{,}600\) which is \(15\%\) of \(24{,}000\) ✓.

questions.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = x^2(x-4)\). How many distinct zeros does \(f\) have?
questions.explanation:
To find the zeros, set \(f(x) = 0\).
$$x^2(x-4) = 0$$
By the Zero Product Property: \(x^2 = 0 \Rightarrow x = 0\) (a double root) or \(x - 4 = 0 \Rightarrow x = 4\).
Although \(x = 0\) is a double root, it counts as only one distinct zero. The function has exactly \(2\) distinct zeros: \(x = 0\) and \(x = 4\).

questions.stem:
The table summarizes data for \(50\) students based on whether they play a sport and whether they are a member of a school club.
\(\text{Club Member}\)\(\text{Not a Club Member}\)\(\text{Total}\)
\(\text{Plays Sport}\)\(12\)\(8\)\(20\)
\(\text{Does Not Play Sport}\)\(18\)\(12\)\(30\)
\(\text{Total}\)\(30\)\(20\)\(50\)
A student who plays a sport is selected at random. What is the probability that this student is a club member?
questions.explanation:
Since the student plays a sport, restrict to the \(20\) students in the “Plays Sport” row. Of those, \(12\) are club members.
$$P(\text{club member} \mid \text{plays sport}) = \frac{12}{20} = \frac{3}{5}$$

questions.stem: A quality control inspector examined \(4{,}800\) items produced at a factory. Of these, \(312\) items were found to be defective. What percent of the items inspected were defective?
questions.explanation:
Divide the number of defective items by the total number of items inspected.
$$\frac{312}{4{,}800} = 0.065 = 6.5\%$$

questions.stem: Triangle \(RST\) is similar to triangle \(XYZ\), where angle \(R\) corresponds to angle \(X\). If \(RS = 9\), \(ST = 12\), and \(XY = 15\), what is the length of \(YZ\)?
questions.explanation:
The ratio of corresponding sides is \(\dfrac{XY}{RS} = \dfrac{15}{9} = \dfrac{5}{3}\). Apply this ratio to find \(YZ\).
$$YZ = 12 \times \frac{5}{3} = 20$$

questions.stem:
$$2x + 3y = 17$$
$$x + y = 7$$
The solution to the given system of equations is \((x, y)\). What is the value of \(x + y\)?
questions.explanation:
Multiply the second equation by \(2\) and subtract from the first.
$$\begin{aligned}2x+3y &= 17 \\ -(2x+2y &= 14) \\ y &= 3\end{aligned}$$
Substitute \(y = 3\) into \(x + y = 7\): \(x = 4\).
$$x + y = 4 + 3 = 7$$

questions.stem:
$$2x^2 - 10x + 8 = 0$$
What is the sum of all solutions to the given equation?
questions.explanation:
Divide the equation by \(2\) to simplify, then apply Vieta’s formula: for \(x^2 + bx + c = 0\), the sum of the roots is \(-b\).
$$x^2 - 5x + 4 = 0$$
$$\text{Sum of roots} = -(-5) = 5$$

questions.stem:
$$6x - 9y = 15$$
$$-4x + ky = -10$$
In the given system of equations, \(k\) is a constant. For what value of \(k\) does the system have infinitely many solutions?
questions.explanation:
A system has infinitely many solutions when both equations represent the same line. Divide the first equation by \(-\frac{3}{2}\) to match the second.
$$\frac{6x - 9y}{-3/2} = \frac{15}{-3/2} \implies -4x + 6y = -10$$
Comparing with \(-4x + ky = -10\), the value of \(k\) must be \(6\).

questions.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are constants. If \(f(1) = 7\) and \(f(2) = 18\), what is the value of \(f(3)\)?
questions.explanation:
Use the two conditions to set up a system of equations.
$$\begin{aligned}f(1) = a + b &= 7 \\ f(2) = 4a + 2b &= 18\end{aligned}$$
From the first equation, \(b = 7 - a\). Substitute into the second.
$$\begin{aligned}4a + 2(7-a) &= 18 \\ 2a &= 4 \\ a &= 2,\ b = 5\end{aligned}$$
$$f(3) = 2(9) + 5(3) = 18 + 15 = 33$$

questions.stem:
$$y = 3$$
$$y = x^2 - 8x + a$$
In the given system of equations, \(a\) is a positive constant. The system has exactly one distinct real solution. What is the value of \(a\)?
questions.explanation:
Substitute \(y = 3\) into the second equation and set equal to zero.
$$0 = x^2 - 8x + (a-3)$$
For exactly one real solution, the discriminant equals zero.
$$\begin{aligned}(-8)^2 - 4(1)(a-3) &= 0 \\ 64 - 4a + 12 &= 0 \\ a &= 19\end{aligned}$$

questions.stem: A circle in the \(xy\)-plane has center \((2, -3)\). If the point \((6, 0)\) lies on the circle, what is the radius of the circle?
questions.explanation:
The radius is the distance from the center to any point on the circle. Use the distance formula.
$$\begin{aligned}r &= \sqrt{(6-2)^2 + (0-(-3))^2} \\ &= \sqrt{16 + 9} \\ &= \sqrt{25} = 5\end{aligned}$$
